description: Dope by Complex, the winner of the PC demo competition at The Gathering 1995, running from its original files in your browser.
about: Dope is Complex's demo for MS-DOS, which won the PC demo competition at The Gathering 1995, held from 11 to 15 April 1995 in Stavanger, Norway. This is its final release, dated 15 April 1995.
Its readme calls it “a bit” unfinished: it was to end with a scroller, for which there was no time to draw graphics, so the readme gives the credits instead.
released: The Gathering 1995: first in the PC demo competition. The final release is dated 15 April 1995.
credits: Code by jmagic; graphics and music by jugi; boxes sketched by jugi and pixelled by reward, the Media Labs logo by reward; 3D objects by jugi and M. Hakulinen, the cat's “found from some cdrom...”; music replay routine by phantom of Sonic PC, its GUS unit reworked by jmagic (DOPE.TXT).
terms: None found: DOPE.TXT and FILE_ID.DIZ state none, and neither does Complex's site. Rights holders can reach DosKit's owner below.
accuracy: It runs at the device's maximum speed: at a fixed 30,000 cycles its later parts fall seconds behind a capture made on a Pentium III with a Gravis UltraSound, and at maximum cycles they keep pace within a few seconds, on a fast enough device.
It plays only through the Gravis UltraSound, which DosKit gives it.
Its end has not been seen in DosKit, and only its first four minutes have been checked for flashing.
Mono: js-dos mixes the Gravis UltraSound's two channels into one.
imageAlt: Dope's blue metallic tubes, running in DosKit
